{{Short description|Finnish mathematician and statistician (born 1943)}}
'''Elja Arjas''' (born February 9, 1943, in [[Tampere]]) is a Finnish mathematician and statistician. He is professor emeritus at the [[University of Helsinki]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Corander |first=Jukka |date=2022-09-30 |title=A conversation with Elja Arjas (Helsinki, November 2021 and March 2022) |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/sjos.12612 |journal=Scandinavian Journal of Statistics |volume=50 |language=en |pages=3–12 |doi=10.1111/sjos.12612 |hdl=10852/99365 |s2cid=252094117 |issn=0303-6898|hdl-access=free }}</ref>

== Education and career ==
Arjas studied mathematics at the [[University of Helsinki]] and graduated with a bachelor's degree in philosophy in 1964. He graduated with a [[Licentiate (degree)|licentiate]] in mathematics and statistics in 1970 and received his doctorate in mathematics in 1972, under the supervision of [[Olli Lokki]] and [[Gustav Elfving]]. He was a research fellow at the [[Center for Operations Research and Econometrics]] at the [[Université catholique de Louvain]] until 1973, before moving back to Finland.<ref name=CV>{{Cite web |title=Elja Arjas - Biometry Research Group at the Department of Mathematics and Statistics - University of Helsinki Confluence |url=https://wiki.helsinki.fi/display/biometry/Elja+Arjas |access-date=2022-12-20 |website=wiki.helsinki.fi}}</ref>

Arjas was a professor of applied mathematics and statistics at the [[University of Oulu]] between 1975 and 1997. Between 1992 and 1997, he worked as an academy professor at the [[Academy of Finland]], and from 1997 to 2009 as a part-time professor of biometrics at the [[University of Helsinki]] and as a research professor at the Institute of Health and Welfare. Arjas was a visiting professor at the [[University of British Columbia]] between 1978 and 1979, a visiting professor at the [[University of Washington]] and the [[Fred Hutchinson Cancer Research Center]] from 1984 to 1985.<ref name=CV />

== Honors and awards ==
Arjas was elected a fellow of the [[International Statistical Institute]] in 1977, a fellow of the a member of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]] in 1982, and a member of the [[Finnish Academy of Sciences]] in 2001. He received an honorary doctorate from the [[University of Oulu]] in 2006.<ref name=CV />
